title: 《高等微積分》第 0 集｜這本書是什麼｜Loomis & Sternberg 全書導論
description:
這是 Loomis 與 Sternberg《Advanced Calculus》系列的第 0 集，先講清楚這本書是什麼、要怎麼讀。

書名叫「高等微積分」，但它不是一般大學裡那門算偏導數與重積分的課。作者 Lynn H. Loomis 與 Shlomo Sternberg 是哈佛大學數學系的教授，這本書出自他們在一九六零年代開的榮譽班講義，一九六八年由 Addison-Wesley 出版，一九九零年由 Jones and Bartlett 出修訂版。

序言把先修條件寫得很清楚：嚴格觀點下的單變數微積分、一些線性代數、熟悉極限與連續這類論證，以及對偏導數的一點經驗。作者建議的入門書是 Courant、Apostol、Spivak 與 Hardy。

全書大致分成兩半。前半把微分學整個建立在賦範向量空間上，後半處理可微流形上的微積分。核心的觀念轉換在於：初等微積分裡導數是一個數，是切線的斜率；在這本書裡，微分是一個線性映射，是最接近真實變化量的那一個線性逼近，而它與真實變化的差比位移本身還要小一個等級。

本集逐章走過全書結構：
第 0 到 2 章 —— 邏輯、量詞、集合，以及向量空間、對偶空間、矩陣、跡與行列式。
第 3 章 —— 全書前半的重心，從範數與連續性、無窮小的三個類、微分與方向導數，一路到隱函數定理與拉格朗日乘子。
第 4 到 6 章 —— 度量空間、緊緻性、完備性、壓縮映射不動點定理，純量積空間，以及微分方程與傅立葉級數。
第 7 到 8 章 —— 多重線性泛函、交錯張量與外代數，以及黎曼積分的公理化理論與變數變換公式。
第 9 到 11 章 —— 可微流形、切空間、向量場與李導數，流形上的積分與散度定理，最後匯集到外微積分與斯托克斯定理。序言提醒第 9 章是學生最難吸收的一章。
第 12 到 13 章 —— 兩章互相獨立的應用：位勢論，以及用辛幾何重講一次古典力學。

本系列會照著書的順序走，大約兩到四個書頁做成一集，加星號的進階節也不跳過，全書預計一百六十九集。下一集從第 0 章第 1 到 3 節開始，講邏輯與量詞。

本影片為雙語教學動畫系列（繁體中文版）。

title: Advanced Calculus, Episode 0 | What This Book Is | Loomis & Sternberg, an overview
description:
This is episode 0 of a series on Loomis and Sternberg's Advanced Calculus, setting out what the book is and how to read it.

The cover says Advanced Calculus, but this is not the usual course in partial derivatives and multiple integrals. Lynn H. Loomis and Shlomo Sternberg were both in the Harvard mathematics department, and the book grew out of an honors course they gave in the nineteen sixties. It was published by Addison-Wesley in 1968, with a revised edition from Jones and Bartlett in 1990.

The preface states the prerequisites plainly: one variable calculus from a rigorous point of view, some linear algebra, comfort with limit and continuity arguments, and a little experience with partial derivatives. It suggests Courant, Apostol, Spivak and Hardy as introductory texts.

The book divides roughly in half. The first half develops the calculus entirely in the setting of normed vector spaces; the second deals with the calculus of differentiable manifolds. The central shift is this: in elementary calculus the derivative is a number, the slope of the tangent line. Here the differential is a linear map, the one linear approximation closest to the actual change, and the gap between them is of smaller order than the displacement.

The episode walks through the structure chapter by chapter:
Chapters 0 to 2 — logic, quantifiers and sets, then vector spaces, the dual space, matrices, trace and determinant.
Chapter 3 — the heart of the first half, from norms and continuity through infinitesimals, the differential and directional derivatives, to the implicit-function theorem and Lagrange multipliers.
Chapters 4 to 6 — metric spaces, compactness, completeness and the contraction mapping fixed-point theorem; scalar product spaces; differential equations and Fourier series.
Chapters 7 to 8 — multilinear functionals, alternating tensors and the exterior algebra; the axiomatic theory of Riemann integration and the change of variables formula.
Chapters 9 to 11 — differentiable manifolds, tangent spaces, vector fields and Lie derivatives, integration on manifolds and the divergence theorem, gathering into exterior calculus and Stokes' theorem. The preface warns that chapter 9 is the one students find hardest.
Chapters 12 to 13 — two independent applications: potential theory, and classical mechanics redone with symplectic geometry.

The series follows the book in order, at roughly two to four printed pages per episode, and does not skip the starred advanced sections, coming to about 169 episodes. The next one starts at chapter 0, sections 1 to 3, with logic and quantifiers.

Part of a bilingual animated teaching series (English edition).
